faqs.answer: Evening tour. We pick you up around 6:30–7pm, when Accra's night food scene starts coming alive.
faqs.question: What time does this tour start?

faqs.answer: Typically 4–6 stops — a mix of street stalls, chop bars, and local restaurants that Accra residents actually eat at, far from hotel buffets.
faqs.question: How many food stops are there?

faqs.answer: Plenty. You'll leave full. Each stop is a real portion, not a small bite.
faqs.question: Will there be enough food?

faqs.answer: Yes. Let us know when booking and we'll ensure each stop has solid vegetarian options ready.
faqs.question: Are vegetarian options available?

faqs.answer: Completely. Our guides take you only to vendors they know personally — high turnover, fresh ingredients, loyal local crowds.
faqs.question: Is it safe to eat street food?

faqs.answer: Casual and comfortable. This is a street crawl, not a sit-down dinner. Wear clothes you can move freely in.
faqs.question: What should I wear?

content.overview: From waakye stalls to kelewele vendors and rooftop bars - taste Accra's legendary food scene as the city lights up at night.

good_to_know.text: Waakye — rice and beans cooked together — is one of Ghana's most beloved street foods. The reddish color comes from dried sorghum leaves added during cooking.
Kelewele (spiced fried plantain) is believed to have West African roots going back centuries, spiced with a blend that varies by vendor and family.
Accra's night food scene centers around neighborhoods like Osu, Labone, and Adabraka — each with its own street food identity and loyal local crowd.

seo.title: Volta Community Tour | People & Places Tours

faqs.answer: The Volta Day Tour is the sights: Mount Gemi, the monkey sanctuary and Wli. This one is the people: farms, palm wine, distilling and cocoa, with Wli at the end.
faqs.question: How is this different from the Volta Day Tour?

faqs.answer: Yes. Tasting the palm wine and the akpeteshie is part of the day. Anything you want to buy and take home is not.
faqs.question: Is the palm wine tasting included?

faqs.answer: Four to five hours each way, so we leave Accra very early to make the most of the daylight.
faqs.question: How long is the drive?

faqs.answer: About thirty minutes on a forest path to the lower falls. Regular fitness is fine, and it can be slippery in the wet season.
faqs.question: Is there a hike to the waterfall?

faqs.answer: Yes, and it is welcome. Anything you buy is between you and them, and is not part of the tour price.
faqs.question: Can I buy from the farmers?

faqs.answer: Walking shoes, a light rain jacket, sun protection and cash for anything you want to buy from the producers.
faqs.question: What should I bring?

content.overview: A day with the people who grow and make things in the Volta Region: palm wine harvested and distilled into akpeteshie, palm oil pressed, cocoa picked, and Wli Waterfalls to finish.

good_to_know.text: Akpeteshie is distilled from fermented palm wine and was banned under colonial rule.
Ghana was the world's largest cocoa producer for much of the twentieth century.
Wli Waterfalls is the highest in West Africa.
